cases.purpose: Root prepares files and directories owned by another unprivileged uid (2002:3002), by root, and by uid 2000 with a non-member group 3002; a nested shell of the same side then runs chmod as uid/gid 2000 with no supplementary groups: denial on foreign-owned files and directories (status, diagnostic, unchanged mode), silent S_ISGID dropping by the kernel for g+s and 2755/2775 on the caller's own files and directories in a non-member group, a member-group control, and a mixed operand list.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 chmod run by the same uid in the same layout
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per chmod with status and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix, then /usr/bin/stat %n %a %u:%g of every fixture; file modes are also compared in the tree snapshot.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 0755 own
/usr/bin/touch own/other own/rootf own/mine-fg own/mine
/usr/bin/mkdir own/otherdir own/mydir-fg
/usr/bin/chown 2002:3002 own/other own/otherdir; /usr/bin/chown 0:0 own/rootf
/usr/bin/chown 2000:3002 own/mine-fg own/mydir-fg; /usr/bin/chown 2000:2000 own/mine
/usr/bin/chmod 0644 own/other own/rootf own/mine-fg own/mine; /usr/bin/chmod 0755 own/otherdir own/mydir-fg
u other-0600 'chmod 0600 own/other'
u other-u+x 'chmod u+x own/other'
u rootf-0600 'chmod 0600 own/rootf'
u otherdir-0700 'chmod 0700 own/otherdir'
u otherdir-g+s 'chmod g+s own/otherdir'
u mine-fg-g+s 'chmod g+s own/mine-fg'
u mine-fg-2755 'chmod 2755 own/mine-fg'
u mydir-fg-g+s 'chmod g+s own/mydir-fg'
u mydir-fg-2775 'chmod 2775 own/mydir-fg'
u mine-2755 'chmod 2755 own/mine'
u mixed 'chmod 0640 own/mine own/other own/mine-fg'
/usr/bin/stat -c '%n %a %u:%g' own/other own/otherdir own/rootf own/mine-fg own/mydir-fg own/mine

cases.purpose: chown with CAP_CHOWN to uids and gids distinct from the caller, numeric and named through a synthetic passwd/group database bind-mounted in the side's mount namespace: user only, group only, user:group, and a symlink with -h (link changes, target unchanged) and without -h (target changes); resulting ids read with /usr/bin/stat.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 chown as root with the same database
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per chown (status, diagnostic minus the shell-location prefix), then /usr/bin/stat %n %u:%g of every file and link (lstat for links).

cases.purpose: Root creates a sticky world-writable directory owned by uid 2002 holding a 0600 file, a 0666 file and a setuid file of that uid, reads fs.protected_hardlinks, sets it to 1 and then 0, and restores it (also on exit); a nested shell runs link as uid 2000: with policy 1 the unreadable and setuid sources are refused with EPERM and no destination while the read-write source is allowed, and with policy 0 both are allowed.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 link run by the same uid with the same policy
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: the policy before, at each step and after restore, one line per link (status, diagnostic minus the shell-location prefix), /usr/bin/stat link counts and ownership, and the destination listing; the tree snapshot compares the resulting files.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
orig=$(< /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks)
trap 'echo "$orig" > /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks' EXIT
echo "protected_hardlinks before=$orig"
/usr/bin/install -d -m 1777 -o 2002 -g 3002 sticky
/usr/bin/install -m 0600 -o 2002 -g 3002 /dev/null sticky/secret
/usr/bin/install -m 0666 -o 2002 -g 3002 /dev/null sticky/open
/usr/bin/install -m 4755 -o 2002 -g 3002 /dev/null sticky/setuid
/usr/bin/install -d -m 0777 dest
echo 1 > /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks; echo "policy=$(< /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks)"
u p1-unreadable 'link sticky/secret dest/l1'
u p1-readwrite 'link sticky/open dest/l2'
u p1-setuid 'link sticky/setuid dest/l3'
echo 0 > /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks; echo "policy=$(< /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks)"
u p0-unreadable 'link sticky/secret dest/l4'
u p0-setuid 'link sticky/setuid dest/l5'
echo "$orig" > /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks; trap - EXIT
echo "restored=$(< /proc/sys/fs/protected_hardlinks)"
/usr/bin/stat -c '%n %h %u:%g %a' sticky sticky/secret sticky/open sticky/setuid
/usr/bin/ls dest

cases.purpose: Root (CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE) marks a regular file on the side's scratch tmpfs immutable; unlink by relative and absolute path is refused even for root, the entry and its contents remain, teardown clears the flag (read back with lsattr) and the file can then be unlinked.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: flags via /usr/bin/lsattr, one line per unlink (status, diagnostic minus the shell-location prefix), the directory listing and content after the denial, and the final listing.

cases.purpose: On a loop-mounted ext4 image: uid 2000 without CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE is refused +i and +a and succeeds with -i/-a no-ops; root sets +i (append and unlink then fail) and clears it, sets +a (truncating write fails, append succeeds) and clears it; a failing inner script leaves +i/+a set and a chattr -R -ia cleanup clears them. Nothing outlives the side: the image and mount live in its private namespaces.
cases.oracle: e2fsprogs 1.47.2 chattr, flags read with e2fsprogs lsattr
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr. Each line reports one invocation: its status, stdout and its diagnostic with any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix removed. Flags are read back with /usr/bin/lsattr -d (e2fsprogs, the same independent reader on both sides) on a fresh 4 MiB ext4 image (no journal) loop-mounted in the side's private mount namespace, outside the compared tree; the image and mount are destroyed with the side.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
I=/tmp/root-fixture.img M=/tmp/root-fixture-mnt
/usr/bin/truncate -s 4M $I && /usr/sbin/mkfs.ext4 -q -F -O ^has_journal $I && /usr/bin/mkdir $M && /usr/bin/mount -o loop $I $M || { echo SETUP-FAILED; exit 99; }
cd $M
lsa() { for f in "$@"; do /usr/bin/lsattr -d "$f" 2>&1 | /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //'; done | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; echo; }
printf 'a\n' > f; printf 'a\n' > g; /usr/bin/chown 2000:2000 f g; /usr/bin/chmod 0777 .
u nocap+i 'chattr +i f'
u nocap+a 'chattr +a f'
u nocap-i 'chattr -i f'
u nocap-a 'chattr -a f'
echo "nocap flags: $(lsa f)"
r cap+i chattr +i f
echo "flags: $(lsa f)"
( echo more >> f ) 2>/dev/null; echo "append-to-immutable status=$?"
/usr/bin/rm -f f 2>/dev/null; echo "unlink-immutable status=$? exists=$([[ -e f ]] && echo y)"
r cap-i chattr -i f
r cap+a chattr +a g
echo "flags: $(lsa g)"
( echo over > g ) 2>/dev/null; echo "truncate-append-only status=$?"
( echo more >> g ) 2>/dev/null; echo "append status=$? content=$(/usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < g)"
r cap-a chattr -a g
"$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'chattr +i f; chattr +a g; exit 3'; echo "failing inner script status=$?"
echo "left by failing script: $(lsa f g)"
r cleanup chattr -R -ia .
echo "after cleanup: $(lsa f g)"
cd /tmp/parity-case && /usr/bin/umount $M && /usr/bin/rm -f $I && echo teardown=ok
